newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel steady, jet bid higher.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet- Diesel steady, jet bid higher.

text.p: Singapore physical gas oil market was steady, resisting a further fall while jet fuel was actively bid at higher prices, traders said on Friday.
Gas oil was heard traded at a low 33-cent per barrel discount fob, but some traders said the price appeared too low adding that it should be at least at parity to Singapore spot quotes fob.

Another cargo was sold by a Singapore trader to a European major at $25.30 a barrel for second-half February lifting fob. A major who has been offering several cargoes at around $26.00 throughout this week was not seen today.
Traders said the absence of demand from China has even forced oil majors in Hong Kong to turn away cargoes as storage terminal in the colony are full.
Swaps for February traded as high as $26.25 per barrel earlier, up about 30 cents from Thursday, but traded lower late in the day at $25.90.

It became apparent that the shortage of jet fuel in Asia was also due to arbitrage cargoes being moved to the U.S. West Coast from South Korea and Japan. But the recent price rally has forced the arbitrage to shut again.
The arbitrage cargoes were heard sold around $1.00 per barrel to Singapore spot quotes fob S.Korea and Japan.
Premiums to Japan on a cost-and-freight basis has now surged to $2.25 a barrel, traders said.

Three buyers emerged for second-half February jet fuel at $31.00-$31.30, dismissing earlier talk that the market would not breach the $31.00-mark, after a deal was done on Thursday at $30.75 a barrel.
Sellers were absent from the market on Friday as supplies were scarce. Traders said the market remained well-supported by several players.
